spec_match.rationale: Contrasts a free pan against an axis-locked pan on the same map, tracing each pane's actual scroll path so the locked gesture's corner is visible.

interactive.rationale: Buttons drive programmatic pans and the traced paths rendered; pointer panning available for real-input users.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The one-movement-vs-two framing is exactly what the traces show.

edge_cases.rationale: Notes that programmatic scrolls are not gesture-locked, which is why the pointer path matters — honest about what headless/mouse input can show.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Programmatic path demo exercised; console clean; both viewports clean.

accessibility.rationale: Buttons named, canvas paths paired with textual readouts, visible focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px overflow; touch is the native input for the demo on mobile.

openQuestions.title: Capture a real touch-gesture trace on a device
openQuestions.detail: Axis locking is a compositor decision about real gestures; headless programmatic scrolling cannot trigger it. Verify the locked-path rendering with a real touch drag (devtools device emulation with touch, or a phone) and record whether the lock signature appears, then refresh this critique.

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 screenshots captured and inspected — programmatic paths only; the real-gesture branch needs a touch-capable session to confirm.
